w10_P4_002250: A tramway depot tests a car of mass 25000 g on its scale rig. The car's speed, in metres per second, is 4 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 15 times x, plus 56, equals exactly 0. The depot's inspection pit is 18 m long. The depot's sheet takes the car's kinetic energy in kilojoules and adds 22 kJ drawn by the substation. Ten identical cars run on the line, and the report gives 10 times the single-car figure. What does the report give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002251: A laboratory air track carries a glider of mass 11000 g. The glider's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 10 times the value, plus 16, equals exactly 0. Four identical gliders run on the track at once, so the track total is 4 times one glider's energy. Expressed in kilojoules, the bench sheet then subtracts 1 kJ drawn by the blower, and the lab runs a mirrored second bench, doubling the figure. What does the lab's sheet give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002255: A shipyard's site figure is a yard total less 1 kN allowed for the tie-down bolts. The yard total is 5 times a bay's force, and each bay carries 7 identical hoists, so a bay's force is 7 times one hoist's force in kilonewtons. One hoist drives a load of mass 74 kg. That load's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the hoist's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 1st second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 7 times t. What is the shipyard's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002256: A cable-tension rig's report is a bank total less 13 kN for the frame's own reaction. The bank total is 11 times a single actuator's corrected force, and an actuator's corrected force is the force on its load in kilonewtons plus 5 kN for the anchor plate. The load has a mass of 49000 g. Its speed along the guide, in metres per second, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 0 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the rig takes how fast that speed is changing at the instant 3 seconds in as the load's acceleration. What does the rig's report give, in kN?
w10_P4_002260: A packing hall's floor figure is a plant total less 21 N for the load-cell offset. The plant total is 9 times a bank's force, and each bank has 9 identical pushers working together. One pusher drives a tray of mass 47000 g. That tray's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 9 times the value, plus 20, equals exactly 0. What is the hall's floor figure, in N?
w10_P4_002262: A furniture works receives 171 brackets of one type and 265 of another, and it packs them into identical cartons using the largest carton size that divides both counts exactly. A test sled of mass 118000 g is then driven at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that carton size. Four identical sleds are pushed on the same frame, so the frame takes 4 times the single-sled force. The works' log then subtracts 21 N for the rail drag. What does the log give, in kN?
w10_P4_002265: A gantry crane test rig drives a block of mass 76000 g. The block's acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the rig's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 3rd second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 3 times t squared plus 3 times t. Ten identical blocks hang from each gantry, and the yard operates 11 gantries. The yard's sheet then subtracts 22 kN allowed for the rail restraint. What does the yard's sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002266: A workshop's hall figure is 7 times a bench's balance, because seven identical benches run together. A bench's balance is the driving force in kilonewtons, less 15 kN allowed for the granite base and then plus 25 kN for the tie-down frame. The driven slide has a mass of 62000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, equals exactly 0. What is the workshop's hall figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002267: A test bench's final entry takes an energy figure, subtracts 9 J for the release catch, adds 17 J credited to the sensor supply, and then subtracts 19 J for the brake. That energy figure is the kinetic energy of a puck of mass 23 kg. The puck's speed, in metres per second, equals the total the bench's meter accumulates between the 0th and the 2nd second. The meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 5 times t squared plus 2 times t. What is the bench's final entry, in J?
w10_P4_002269: A mine hoist's total is 8 times a shaft figure, and each shaft figure is 8 times the force on a single skip, because eight skips hang on every rope set. A skip has a mass of 46 kg. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 9 times a number x, with 1 then added. That number x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 7 times x, plus 6, equals exactly 0. What is the mine hoist's total, in N?
w10_P4_002270: A physics bench releases a cart of mass 12 kg along a level rail. The cart's speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 6, equals exactly 0. The bench's lamp draws 55 W. Expressed in kilojoules, the bench sheet takes the cart's kinetic energy, subtracts 13 kJ drawn by the pump, adds 28 kJ supplied from the mains, and then subtracts 3 kJ for the datalogger. What does the bench sheet total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002275: A bridge-jacking contractor's site figure is 11 times a pier's balance. A pier's balance is the jacking force in kilonewtons, plus 21 kN for the packing plates and then less 10 kN credited to the bearing shims. The jack drives a mass of 196000 g. That mass's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by adding together the squares of each whole number from 1 to 4. What is the contractor's site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002276: A rolling plant's group figure is 8 times a works total, and the works total is a mill figure plus 10 N for the load-pin offset. A mill figure is 9 times a stand's force, and a stand carries 3 identical rolls pushing together. One roll drives a mass of 85 kg, and that mass's position along the guide, in metres, is 5 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 6 times the square of the elapsed seconds; the plant reads how fast it is moving at the instant 1 second in and takes that number as the acceleration in metres per second squared. The plant's cooling tower is rated at 200 kW. What is the plant's group figure, in N?
w10_P4_002278: A conveyor works drives a pallet of mass 140000 g. The pallet's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 5 times the value, plus 6, equals exactly 0. Five identical pallets run on each lane, and the lane log then adds 20 N for the belt drag. Three lanes make up a bank, and the works runs 6 identical banks. What total force do the works' drives supply, in N?
w10_P4_002283: A skate park's log gives a session figure in kilojoules, covering the 6 identical runs made in a session. A single run's booked energy is the rider's kinetic energy plus 4 J for the timing gate. The rider and board together have a mass of 17000 g. Their speed at the bottom of the ramp, in metres per second, is the larger of the two values whose square, minus 12 times the value, plus 32, equals exactly 0. What does the log give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002285: A depot's balance is a paired figure in kilojoules, less 13 kJ drawn by the compressor. The paired figure is twice the energy of a single trolley, since the trolleys always run in pairs. A trolley has a mass of 54000 g, and the depot's inspection lamp draws 70 W. A trolley's speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 364 and 295 exactly. What does the depot's balance give, in kJ?
w10_P4_002287: A wind-turbine yard drives a test mass of 17000 g on its jacking rig. That mass's position along the guide, in metres, is 4 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the yard reads how fast it is moving at the instant 1 second in, taking that number as the acceleration in metres per second squared. The yard's sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons and adds 14 kN for the base flange. Nine identical rigs work each tower, and the yard erects 3 towers at once. What total does the yard's sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002294: A cable-car company's fleet figure is 4 times a line's figure, and a line's figure is twice a cabin's booked energy, because the cabins run in pairs. A cabin's booked energy is its kinetic energy in kilojoules plus 29 kJ drawn by the haulage house. A cabin has a mass of 40 kg on the scale model used for the estimate. Its distance along the model track, in metres, is 2 times the cube of the elapsed seconds minus 1 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the company uses how fast it is moving at the instant 3 seconds in. What is the company's fleet figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002295: A survey frame drives a mass of 55 kg on its slide. The slide's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is numerically equal to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from the frame's 6 mounting eyes, taking 2 at a time. The frame's beacon draws 35 W. The site sheet takes the driving force in kilonewtons, subtracts 15 kN allowed for the ballast block, and then subtracts a further 27 kN for the ground anchors. What does the site sheet give, in kN?
w10_P4_002298: A theatre rigging company's tour figure is 7 times a venue's balance, because seven identical venues are fitted out. A venue's balance is a truss force in kilonewtons, less 26 kN allowed for the roof steelwork. A truss force is 5 times a single motor's force, since five motors lift each truss. One motor drives a load of mass 24 kg at an acceleration, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to the number of different groups of 4 that can be chosen from the truss's 7 pick-up points. What is the company's tour figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002300: A bobsleigh centre launches a sled of mass 47000 g. The sled's speed, in metres per second, is 4 times a number x, where x is the smaller of the two values for which x squared, minus 14 times x, plus 48, equals exactly 0. The centre's start hut is lit by a 60 W lamp. Seven identical sleds are launched in each heat. How much energy does a heat account for, in kJ?
w10_P4_002301: A demolition contractor's regional figure is 11 times a site's force, expressed in kilonewtons. A site's force is 4 times a rig's force, and each rig carries 9 identical breakers working together. One breaker drives a tool of mass 22000 g, and the rig's dust suppressor is rated at 5 kW. The tool's position along the guide, in metres, is 3 times the cube of the elapsed seconds plus 4 times the square of the elapsed seconds, and the contractor reads how fast the tool's velocity is changing at the instant 4 seconds in to get its acceleration. What is the contractor's regional figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002302: A bench's final reading is a session total less 14 J for the timing gate. The session total is 6 times a single run's net figure, and a run's net figure is the puck's kinetic energy less 23 J drawn by the air blower. The puck has a mass of 55 kg. Its speed, in metres per second, is numerically equal to the largest whole number that divides both 64 and 333 exactly. What is the bench's final reading, in J?
w10_P4_002304: A quayside crane meters its hoist through a lift, and at time t seconds the meter's instantaneous rate is 4 times t squared plus 7 times t. The crane takes the total accumulated between the 1st and the 3rd second and subtracts 17 to obtain the load's acceleration in metres per second squared. The load has a mass of 66 kg, and the crane's jib reaches 30 m. The log adds 22 N for the sheave friction, and the quay works two identical cranes on the same lift, doubling the figure. What does the log record, in kN?
w10_P4_002307: A dry-dock operator's yard figure is 12 times a single caisson's balance, expressed in kilonewtons. A caisson's balance is the driving force plus 13 kN for the seal ring and then a further 18 kN for the guide shoes. The caisson has a mass of 170 kg on the scale rig used for the estimate. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, equals the total the rig's meter accumulates between the 2nd and the 4th second, where the meter's instantaneous rate at time t seconds is 2 times t squared plus 5 times t. What is the operator's yard figure, in kN?
